title: perf(workboard): paginate card and session board responses

commit.messageHeadline: perf(usage): reuse overview snapshots and avoid transcript replay
perf(workboard): paginate card and session board responses
chore: integrate main usage test fixtures
fix(usage): retain canonical admission for inventory reads
fix(workboard): satisfy paging types and lint contracts
test(usage): prepare runtime config for admission regression
fix(workboard): keep paged widget cards visible
chore: merge main into usage scaling

Two P2 follow-ups from the automated review remain under this campaign's two-round review limit:

- A refresh that rebuilds more than one card page can repeat a card if another client moves it across the cursor between reads. Deduplicate refresh-page accumulation by ID, as the Load more path already does. A stable Refresh recovers; no server card is duplicated or lost.
- Dispatch currently reloads the first 100 cards and preserves `nextCursor`, so later loaded cards and their selection leave the visible window. Load more restores the cards. Follow-up: route post-dispatch reconciliation through the existing held-window refresh loader.

Neither changes persisted card data. These visible paging limitations are disclosed rather than adding a consistency generation or cross-request handshake.

Codex review: needs changes before merge. ## What this changes This PR paginates card and Sessions board responses in batches of 100 and adds loading controls to bundled consumers. **Example:** Open a Workboard containing 205 cards. - **Before:** The initial response contains all 205 complete cards. - **After:** The initial response contains 100 cards and a cursor; Load more retrieves subsequent pages. ## Review scores | Measure | Result | What it means | |---|---|---| | **Overall readiness** | 🧂 unranked krab **(1/6)** | The direction is useful and owner-approved, but two confirmed consumer regressions block correctness and required visual/runtime evidence remains pending. | | **Proof confidence** | 🧂 unranked krab **(1/6)** | Real behavior proof is not required for maintainer- or bot-authored pull requests. | | **Patch quality** | 🦪 silver shellfish **(2/6)** | 2 actionable review findings remain. | ## Product **Kind:** Performance · **Worth it:** Yes · **Fix scope:** Complete **User problem:** Large retained boards require expensive complete-population responses whenever their data changes. **Reason:** The feature-history owner explicitly chose pagination and its compatibility tradeoff, and existing user reports establish practical value. ## Merge readiness ⛔ **Needs changes before merge - 2 items remain** Keep open: bounded Workboard responses address a real performance problem, but two paging regressions remain in this PR. **Priority:** P2 **Reviewed head:** `13d2c71c7b1d6d5e57ab543dfc2472ac9bd970a3` ## Before merge - [ ] **Deduplicate continuation pages when refreshing the held window (P2)** - With more than 100 cards loaded, a refresh fetches multiple live pages. If another client moves a card from the first page beyond its cursor before the continuation read, that card appears again. This push preserves both copies, unlike the deduplicating Load more path, so keyed card lists and loaded counts receive duplicate IDs. Accumulate refresh pages by card ID and use the unique count when restoring the held window. This confirms the existing connector review concern. - [ ] **Preserve the loaded card window after dispatch (P2)** - After a user loads 200 cards and selects Start agents, dispatch still requests the default list once and replaces state.cards with its now-bounded 100-card response. Previously loaded later cards disappear, and setWorkboardCards also removes their selections. Retaining nextCursor does not restore that window. Reconcile dispatch through the window-preserving loader or follow continuation pages to the previous unique-card count. This confirms the existing connector review concern. ## Findings - [P2] Deduplicate continuation pages when refreshing the held window — `extensions/workboard/browser/lib/workboard/loading.ts:89-90` - [P2] Preserve the loaded card window after dispatch — `extensions/workboard/browser/lib/workboard/mutations.ts:368-371` ### Tests - Missing end-to-end proof: Supplied evidence does not show the changed board/widget flow through a shipped entry point, inspected before/after screenshots, a stable-release upgrade with existing cards intact, or base-fail/head-pass execution of the added regressions.
Agent review details ### How this fits together The Workboard plugin serves persisted cards and caller-authorized Sessions projections through Gateway RPCs to board pages, dashboard widgets, session accessories, and the CLI. ```mermaid flowchart TD A[Board pages and widgets] --> C[Workboard Gateway RPCs] B[CLI and session accessories] --> C C --> D[Card store and worker] C --> E[Authorized Sessions projection] D --> F[Bounded response pages] E --> F F --> G[Consumer loaded windows] ``` ### Technical review Best possible solution: Keep the plugin-owned pagination design and use one deduplicating loaded-window reconciliation path for refresh and dispatch. Do we have a high-confidence way to reproduce the issue? Source establishes both the unbounded current-main response path and the introduced refresh/dispatch failures; no target code or tests were executed during this read-only review. Is this the best way to solve the issue? Bounding selection and transport at the existing plugin owners is appropriate, while duplicated reconciliation logic leaves two consumer regressions. Full review comments: - [P2] Deduplicate continuation pages when refreshing the held window — `extensions/workboard/browser/lib/workboard/loading.ts:89-90` With more than 100 cards loaded, a refresh fetches multiple live pages. If another client moves a card from the first page beyond its cursor before the continuation read, that card appears again. This push preserves both copies, unlike the deduplicating Load more path, so keyed card lists and loaded counts receive duplicate IDs. Accumulate refresh pages by card ID and use the unique count when restoring the held window. This confirms the existing connector review concern. Confidence: 0.98 Late finding: first raised on code an earlier review cycle already covered. - [P2] Preserve the loaded card window after dispatch — `extensions/workboard/browser/lib/workboard/mutations.ts:368-371` After a user loads 200 cards and selects Start agents, dispatch still requests the default list once and replaces state.cards with its now-bounded 100-card response. Previously loaded later cards disappear, and setWorkboardCards also removes their selections. Retaining nextCursor does not restore that window. Reconcile dispatch through the window-preserving loader or follow continuation pages to the previous unique-card count. This confirms the existing connector review concern. Confidence: 0.99 Late finding: first raised on code an earlier review cycle already covered. Overall correctness: patch is incorrect Overall confidence: 0.97 AGENTS.md: found and applied where relevant. later revision receipts avoid unchanged downloads.) - `Session-linked selection and accessory reads` keeps the original intent (f125842fe77691e619755a97d47706cf1991704b: Keep chat catalog reads out of unrelated card history while preserving complete session-linked results.) - `Sessions board projection and refresh controller` keeps the original intent (df37101311ab410fe0253acce002324be8652de3: Share prepared projections while preserving caller-bound authorization and avoiding unchanged responses.) - `CLI list ownership and complete output` keeps the original intent (c4e70bc82a5f70dd817540b72b139d37975dcb64: Use the running Gateway's store or exclusive offline ownership so CLI results remain current.) - `Board summaries and browser normalization` keeps the original intent (66def08d83293b5a6a1fd1fc9e8b048fd51c992c: Use persisted board records for filter identity and preserve empty-board selection.) - `Card details, dependencies, and dashboard rendering` changes intended behavior with a stated reason (0d4a332ea0c01e668e06ff2d87fdb0a4e6524959: Preserve Workboard behavior and host identities while moving browser rendering to Solid.) ### Testing Proof path: in-process harness. ### Security None. ### Evidence Acceptance criteria: - pnpm --dir ui test --project unit ../extensions/workboard/browser/lib/workboard/index.test.ts - pnpm --dir ui test --project unit ../extensions/workboard/browser/widgets/runtime.test.ts ../extensions/workboard/browser/pages/workboard/workboard-page-sessions.test.ts - pnpm tsgo:extensions - pnpm tsgo:extensions:test - git diff --check What I checked: - **Pinned introduction and accepted direction:** Reviewed the introduced diff from 9154d0c20af050ffc021f0cded3fd461f1b4fd1a to 13d2c71c7b1d6d5e57ab543dfc2472ac9bd970a3. _Reviewed October 17, 2026, 5:06 AM ET / 09:06 UTC._

> Agent-written on behalf of sercada (Claude Code), with production measurements from our gateway.

**Backport request:** could this land in the 2026.10 line (for example 2026.10.10)? Or is it planned only for the first 2026.11 release? Either answer helps us plan.

**Why it matters to us.** This PR fixes the Control UI freeze we measured on 2026.10.7. The full numbers are in https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/186096#issuecomment-6504750368. In short:
- `workboard.cards.list` returned 7.5–7.9 MB per call. That was 92% of all bytes sent to Control UI connections.
- During working hours, 15 of 15 Control UI disconnects (`1006`, `heartbeat-timeout`) came within ~40 s of one of those responses.

**Current status.** Merged to `main` on 2026-10-17. It is not in `2026.10.9` (`latest`) or `2026.10.10-beta.5` (`beta`): the Workboard docs at both tags still have no `after`/`nextCursor`.

**Note for a backport.** On `main`, `workboard.cards.list` now returns at most 100 cards by default. RPC and plugin callers that expect the full list would change behaviour in a patch release. If that is too much for the 2026.10 line, an opt-in variant would still fix the freeze: the server accepts `limit`/`after`, the bundled Control UI uses them, and calls without `limit` keep returning the full list.

Meanwhile we run a downstream workaround: hourly deletion of `done` cards older than 3 days. It cut the list from 7.7 MB to 2.6 MB, but it is a retention policy on our side, not a fix.
